mainTopic: Does שבת make produce obligated in מעשר (קביעות למעשר) even when the produce's processing (גמר מלאכה) is not finished?
overview: This amud opens with the end of the משנה about fruit spread out to dry (מוקצה) that a person wants to eat on שבת. רבי אליעזר says that in שביעית it is enough to say 'from here I will eat tomorrow.' The חכמים require marking the fruit and saying 'from here until here.' The גמרא then quotes two משניות from מסכת מעשרות. In the first, שבת makes figs obligated in מעשר. In the second, a חצר does not make figs obligated while they are still drying. Combining the two, רבא asks רב נחמן whether שבת fixes produce for מעשר even when its work is unfinished. רב נחמן says it does, and he defends this against רבא's comparison to חצר by citing a received teaching (תלמוד ערוך). His son מר זוטרא tries to prove the rule from רבי אליעזר's limit to שביעית. The גמרא rejects that proof: the person's own words 'from here I will eat' may be what fixed the produce. The משנה mentions שבת to teach that טבל still counts as מוכן for שבת, because if someone wrongly tithed it on שבת, it is fixed.

steps.title: End of רבי אליעזר's view: a verbal designation is enough
steps.stepSummary: The משנה concludes רבי אליעזר's ruling. On ערב שבת in שביעית, a person may stand by the drying fruit and say, 'From here I will eat tomorrow.'
steps.simpleTranslation: [רבי אליעזר says: A person may stand by the drying fruit] on ערב שבת during the שביעית year and say: 'From here I will eat tomorrow.'
steps.whatsHappening: We are finishing the משנה's first opinion. According to רבי אליעזר, simply saying out loud which drying fruit you plan to eat is enough to prepare it for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fruit spread out to dry is מוקצה, meaning it is set aside and not ready to eat, so it needs advance preparation (הכנה) before שבת. The case is set in שביעית because that year has no מעשר. That removes the tithing problem and leaves only the question of preparing the fruit for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Friday, the day before שבת
The seventh (Sabbatical) year, when no tithes are taken
'From here I will eat tomorrow': a verbal designation of the fruit

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of the משנה. The opening words 'ועוד אמר רבי אליעזר: עומד אדם על המוקצה' come on the previous amud, so the speaker here is רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: on Shabbat eve during the Sabbatical Year,
phrases.notes: Continues רבי אליעזר's statement from the previous text: a person stands by the drying fruit (מוקצה).

phrases.english: and says: From here I will eat tomorrow.
phrases.notes: Speaking the designation is enough, without any physical marking.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת בַּשְּׁבִיעִית, וְאוֹמֵר: מִכָּאן אֲנִי אוֹכֵל לְמָחָר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, a verbal designation on ערב שבת is enough to prepare drying fruit for use on שבת.

steps.title: The חכמים require marking the fruit
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with רבי אליעזר. A person must physically mark the fruit and say exactly 'from here until here.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: [He may not eat] unless he marks the fruit and says, 'From here until here.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposing view. The חכמים require a physical mark plus a clearly defined boundary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר accepts a general statement. The חכמים want a definite, marked-off portion, so the preparation is clear and specific.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion
That he marks (the fruit)
From here until here: a defined boundary

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute is about how much preparation is needed. רבי אליעזר says speaking is enough. The חכמים say you must mark the fruit and define its limits.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
unless he marks and says:
phrases.notes: Literally 'until he marks', meaning he may not eat it without this.

phrases.english: From here to there.
phrases.notes: A defined section of the fruit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: עַד שֶׁיִּרְשׁוֹם וְיֹאמַר מִכָּאן וְעַד כָּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי אליעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fruit must be marked and clearly bounded on ערב שבת to be usable on שבת.

steps.title: First source: children's hidden figs become obligated in tithes because of שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from מסכת מעשרות. Children hid figs on ערב שבת and forgot to tithe them. Even after שבת, they may not eat them until they tithe.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: Children who hid figs on ערב שבת and forgot and did not tithe them may not eat them even after שבת unless they tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting an outside משנה. This sets up a question that will come shortly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you may snack casually (אכילת עראי) on untithed produce. Because the figs were set aside for eating on שבת, שבת 'fixed' them as obligated in מעשר. That obligation stays even after שבת ends. So the key lesson is that שבת creates קביעות למעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned there, in a משנה elsewhere
They hid
They tithed
After שבת ends

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that שבת fixes produce for מעשר. רבא's question is built on it.

phrases.english: GEMARA: We learned there:
Children who hid figs on Shabbat eve
phrases.notes: They hid them to eat on שבת.

phrases.english: and they forgot and did not tithe —
after Shabbat they may not eat
unless they have tithed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens by bringing in an outside source related to the topic of מוקצה fruit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Produce set aside for שבת becomes obligated in מעשר, and the obligation continues after שבת.

steps.title: Second source: a courtyard does not fix figs that are still drying
steps.stepSummary: A second משנה teaches that figs being moved through a courtyard to dry may be snacked on casually without tithing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we also learned: One who moves figs through his courtyard to dry them, his children and household may snack on them casually and are exempt from tithing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source that seems to point the other way. With two sources in place, it is now ready to ask its question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חצר normally fixes produce for מעשר. Here it does not, because the figs are still drying, so their work is unfinished (לא נגמרה מלאכתן). The lesson is that חצר fixes only produce whose processing is complete.

keyTerms.meaning: And we also learned
Courtyard; normally fixes produce for מעשר
To dry (figs into dried figs)
Casual eating, which is allowed before produce is fixed

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean a חצר never fixes מעשר. It is an exception that applies only because the figs' work is not yet finished.

phrases.english: And we also learned:
One who transfers figs in his courtyard to dry them —
his children and household may eat from them
casually, and they are exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source that limits when קביעות happens.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חצר does not fix produce for מעשר while its work is still unfinished.

steps.title: רבא asks: does שבת fix unfinished produce for tithes?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן whether שבת fixes מוקצה produce for מעשר even when its work is unfinished. One side relies on 'וקראת לשבת עונג'; the other compares שבת to the rule for finished produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן: Does שבת fix מוקצה produce for tithing when its work is not finished? Do we say that since it is written 'And call שבת a delight,' it fixes even unfinished produce? Or perhaps it fixes finished produce but not unfinished produce?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא combines the two sources into one question. Is שבת stronger than a חצר, so that it fixes even unfinished produce?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first side says eating on שבת counts as a delight (עונג), which is a significant meal, so it fixes the produce no matter what stage it is at. The second side says שבת works like other fixers and applies only to produce that is ready.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him
Fixes (makes obligated) for tithing
Its work (processing) is finished
'And call שבת a delight' (ישעיהו 58:13)
Or perhaps

phrases.english: Rava asked Rav Nachman:
Shabbat: does it fix muktze produce for tithing
in an item whose work is not finished?
Do we say, since it is written:
"And call Shabbat a delight",

phrases.aramaic: קָבְעָה וַאֲפִילּוּ בְּדָבָר שֶׁלֹּא נִגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתּוֹ,
phrases.english: it fixes even an item whose work is not finished,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: בְּדָבָר שֶׁנִּגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתּוֹ — קָבְעָה,
phrases.english: or perhaps: an item whose work is finished, it fixes,

phrases.aramaic: בְּדָבָר שֶׁלֹּא נִגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתּוֹ — לָא קָבְעָה?
phrases.english: an item whose work is not finished, it does not fix?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the two sources into a question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether שבת's power to fix produce for מעשר extends to produce whose work is unfinished.

steps.title: רב נחמן: שבת fixes both finished and unfinished produce
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that שבת fixes produce for מעשר whether or not its work is finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: שבת fixes, both an item whose work is finished and an item whose work is not finished.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a direct answer to רבא's question. He follows the first side: שבת is more powerful than a חצר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this answer, שבת differs from חצר. A חצר requires גמר מלאכה, but שבת fixes produce regardless.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him
Fixes, establishes the obligation
Both... and

phrases.english: He said to him: Shabbat fixes,
both an item whose work is finished,
and an item whose work is not finished.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שבת fixes produce for מעשר even when its work is unfinished.

steps.title: רבא challenges: compare שבת to a courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that שבת should be like חצר: just as a courtyard fixes only finished produce, שבת should too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But say שבת is like a courtyard. Just as a courtyard fixes only an item whose work is finished, so too שבת should fix only an item whose work is finished!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רב נחמן's answer with a comparison (a 'מה... אף' argument).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both שבת and חצר are things that fix produce for מעשר. Since the second משנה showed that חצר needs finished work, רבא argues that logic says שבת should follow the same rule.

keyTerms.meaning: But say (introduces a challenge)
Similar to, comparable
Just as... so too (a comparison argument)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְאֵימָא שַׁבָּת דּוּמְיָא דְחָצֵר,
phrases.english: He said to him: But say Shabbat is similar to a courtyard,
just as a courtyard does not fix
except an item whose work is finished,
so too Shabbat should not fix
except an item whose work is finished!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that שבת fixes even unfinished produce.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שבת and חצר are both fixers of מעשר. Since חצר requires finished work, logically שבת should require it too.

steps.title: רב נחמן: this is a received teaching, not my own reasoning
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן replies that he has a fixed, received teaching (תלמוד ערוך) that שבת fixes both finished and unfinished produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We have a fixed teaching in our hands that שבת fixes, both an item whose work is finished and an item whose work is not finished.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his ruling. He explains that it comes from an established tradition, so רבא's logical comparison cannot override it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's comparison is a logical argument. רב נחמן responds that his ruling is not based on logic that can be countered with other logic. It is a received teaching, and a tradition outweighs a comparison argument.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed, established teaching (tradition)
In our hands, meaning we possess it

steps.whatToRemember: שבת fixes produce for מעשר even when its work is unfinished, unlike חצר, which fixes only finished produce. This rule rests on an established teaching, not on reasoning.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תַּלְמוּד עָרוּךְ הוּא בְּיָדֵינוּ
phrases.english: He said to him: We have an established teaching in our hands
that Shabbat fixes,
both an item whose work is finished,
and an item whose work is not finished.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to an established tradition over a logical comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שבת should be like חצר and fix only finished produce.
steps.terutzMaskana: Based on a received teaching, שבת fixes both finished and unfinished produce.

steps.title: מר זוטרא brings support from רבי אליעזר's משנה
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא, the son of רב נחמן, brings a proof from רבי אליעזר's ruling about שביעית. The ruling implies that in other years the produce would be forbidden, because שבת fixes it for מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא, the son of רב נחמן, said: We also learned this in a משנה. 'And רבי אליעזר also said: A person may stand over his מוקצה on ערב שבת in שביעית, etc.' The reason it is allowed is that it is שביעית produce, which is not subject to tithing. That implies that in the other years of the seven-year cycle it would be forbidden. Why? Is it not because שבת fixes it for מעשר?
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא tries to prove his father רב נחמן right from a משנה. He points to the fact that רבי אליעזר's leniency is limited to שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce lying in a מוקצה drying area is unfinished. רבי אליעזר allows it only in שביעית, when there is no מעשר at all. So in a normal year it would need tithing, and the only reason would be that שבת fixed it even though its work was unfinished. That is exactly רב נחמן's position.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it: a proof formula citing a משנה or ברייתא
The seventh, Sabbatical year, whose produce is exempt from מעשר
Subject to tithing
The other years of the seven-year cycle
It fixes, making produce obligated in מעשר before it may be eaten

steps.confusionAlert: Here מוקצה means a storage or drying area for fruit. The fruit in it is also מוקצה for שבת until it is designated (הזמנה), which is why the person must say 'from here I will eat tomorrow.' מר זוטרא uses this case for what it implies about מעשר.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra, son of Rav Nachman, said:
We too have learned it (in a Mishnah):
And Rabbi Eliezer further said:
A person may stand over the drying/storage area
phrases.notes: And designate fruit, saying 'from here I will eat'.

phrases.english: on Shabbat eve in the Sabbatical Year, etc.

phrases.aramaic: טַעְמָא דִּשְׁבִיעִית — דְּלָאו בַּר עַשּׂוֹרֵי הוּא,
phrases.english: The reason is that it is the Sabbatical Year, which is not subject to tithing;

phrases.aramaic: הָא בִּשְׁאָר שְׁנֵי שָׁבוּעַ — הָכִי נָמֵי דְּאָסוּר,
phrases.english: but in the other years of the cycle, it would indeed be forbidden (without tithing).

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא — לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּשַׁבָּת קָבְעָה?
phrases.english: What is the reason? Is it not because Shabbat fixes it (for tithes)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings textual support for רב נחמן's received teaching from Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's rule that שבת fixes even unfinished produce for מעשר
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר's ruling in the משנה about standing over the מוקצה on ערב שבת in שביעית, read for what it implies about other years

steps.title: The proof is rejected: his own words fixed the produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. In רבי אליעזר's case the person declared 'From here I will eat tomorrow,' and that declaration is what fixed the produce, not שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is different there. Since he said 'From here I will eat tomorrow,' he fixed it for himself as a meal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on מר זוטרא's proof. It offers another reason the produce would need tithing in a normal year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Designating the food for a meal is itself an act that fixes produce for מעשר. So the משנה may say nothing about שבת fixing unfinished produce. The tithing obligation could come from the person's own designation.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there: a formula for distinguishing a cited case
From here I will eat tomorrow: the designation statement
He fixed it upon himself, setting it as a meal and so making it obligated in מעשר

phrases.english: No, it is different there,
since he said: 'From here I will eat tomorrow,'
he has fixed it upon himself (as a meal).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 9 by giving a different explanation of the cited case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof only. רב נחמן's rule itself is not disproven.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that שבת caused the tithing obligation. In fact the person's verbal designation could be the cause.

steps.title: Then why does the משנה mention שבת?
steps.stepSummary: If the designation is what fixes the produce, that should work on a weekday too. So why does the משנה specify ערב שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why mention שבת specifically? Even on a weekday it should be the same!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection it just gave. If saying 'I will eat from here' is what fixes the produce, the day should not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The דחיה moved the cause of the obligation from שבת to the person's words. But then the משנה's choice of ערב שבת looks unnecessary. The גמרא demands a reason for that detail.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces a consequence that challenges the previous answer
Why specifically this case? A challenge to a detail that seems unnecessary
A weekday

phrases.english: If so, why specifically Shabbat?
Even on a weekday it should also apply!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the דחיה of Step 10 by pointing to the משנה's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the designation, not שבת, fixed the produce
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the designation alone fixes the produce, it should work on any day. Mentioning ערב שבת then has no purpose.

steps.title: שבת is mentioned to teach that טבל counts as prepared
steps.stepSummary: The משנה mentions שבת to teach that טבל is considered מוכן for שבת. If someone wrongly tithed it on שבת, it is properly fixed and may be eaten, so designating it before שבת is meaningful.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that טבל is considered prepared for שבת. If a person broke the rule and fixed it by tithing, it is fixed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The mention of שבת teaches a separate rule about whether untithed produce counts as prepared for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think that טבל is like מוקצה on שבת, since it may not be tithed or eaten then, so designating it before שבת would mean nothing. The משנה teaches otherwise. Because a person who wrongly tithed it on שבת would end up with fixed produce, טבל is still considered prepared. So the proof for רב נחמן remains rejected, and the משנה's wording is explained.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
Produce from which תרומות and מעשרות have not yet been separated
Prepared, meaning available for use on שבת and not מוקצה
He transgressed and fixed it, separating the tithes on שבת against the rabbinic prohibition

steps.whatToRemember: מר זוטרא's proof for רב נחמן is rejected, because the designation 'from here I will eat' could be what fixed the produce. The mention of שבת in the משנה teaches a separate point: טבל counts as מוכן for שבת, since if it was wrongly tithed on שבת it is fixed.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not permit tithing on שבת. Tithing on שבת remains forbidden. The point is only that if someone did it after the fact, the produce counts as fixed, so טבל is not considered מוקצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out the principle that טבל is not automatically מוקצה on שבת. That principle matters for laws of preparing food for שבת and יום טוב.

phrases.english: This teaches us
that untithed produce is considered prepared with regard to Shabbat,
for if one transgressed and fixed it (by tithing), it is fixed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 11 and keeps the דחיה of Step 10 in place.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New teaching: the detail is explained as teaching a separate rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think טבל is מוקצה on שבת because it cannot be tithed or eaten then, so designating it before שבת would be meaningless.
steps.terutzMaskana: טבל is מוכן for שבת because tithing it after the fact works. So the designation on ערב שבת is valid, and that is why the משנה mentions שבת.
